A non-commercial OS?

questions.asks: English interface?

questions.asks: English available straight after installation?
questions.note: English is the base locale and the fallback for every language but Dutch (lib/pairings_engine_web/locale.ex:39-44,73-75). The desktop build opens the system browser and follows its Accept-Language, so a Dutch browser opens in Dutch; English is one click away (Q9).

questions.asks: English selectable at run time?
questions.note: Language picker in the top bar of every page (lib/pairings_engine_web/components/layouts.ex:250,846-871; router.ex:232), and a per-account language. Off our path while Q8 is YES.

questions.asks: Non-English text inside the English interface?
questions.note: No non-English UI text found in the English catalogue. One placeholder said 'matricule'; it now says 'national ID' (fide_live.ex:784). The opt-in Belgian SWAR results-page export is Dutch by design: a federation upload document, not interface (federations/bel/swar_publish.ex:487-491).

questions.asks: Complete English manual or online help?
questions.note: No user manual and no in-app help: docs/ is developer material, nothing links to it, no /help route.

questions.asks: Manual reachable from inside the program (e.g. F1)?
questions.note: Comes with the manual: a help link on every page. Off our path while Q11 is NO.

questions.asks: Manual available separately (PDF / web link)?
questions.note: Comes with the manual: a PDF per release. Off our path while Q11 is NO.

questions.asks: At least an essential-functions English manual?
questions.note: FAIL - verification stops here. No English manual of the essential functions (rating lists, setup incl. tie-breaks, byes, pairings, printouts); docs/printing.md and docs/pairing-systems.md are developer notes the app does not link.

questions.asks: Commit to completing a partial manual within a year?
questions.note: Only reached with a partial manual; costs 5%. The commitment is the maintainer's to make. Aim for a complete manual instead.

questions.asks: Own pairing and tie-break engine?
questions.note: Ainalrami (pairing) + PairingsEngine.Standings (tie-breaks), both ours.

questions.asks: External engine?
External engine already inside a TAPC'd program?
Checker (PTC) and generator (RTG) available?
questions.note: ainalrami -c (checker) and -g (generator) in the public Apache-2.0 repository (deps/ainalrami/lib/ainalrami/cli.ex:339-349,1464-1526; README.md:222-229). No release binaries: clone, mix escript.build. The form's textbox text (how to get and run them) is still to write.

questions.asks: Checker has a free CLI?
questions.note: ainalrami <file> -c, free, exit codes 0 match / 1 differs / 2 not replayable (cli.ex:348-349,927-940). Built from source.

questions.asks: Checker reads TRF26 and reports wrong pairings per round AND standings that break the tie-breaks?
questions.note: Shipped in Ainalrami 0.30.0, pinned 0.35.0: reads TRF26 (202/212, 192, 250/260), replays every round, and re-ranks by the file's tie-break list, naming every wrong rank in columns 86-89 (cli.ex:948-974,1102-1145,1223-1245). Our own TRF26 exports now pass it, pairings and standings (test/pairings_engine/trf_checker_round_trip_test.exs) - except Baku tournaments, see Q106. Limits: individual colour differences are noted, not counted; a round robin exits 2 (not replayed).

questions.asks: Generator has a free CLI?
questions.note: ainalrami -g (cli.ex:339-340,428-475).

questions.asks: Generator has a free non-CLI interface?
questions.note: Not needed: Q22 is YES.

questions.asks: Generator configures players, rounds, each bye type, forfeit wins/losses, odd results, BAM, tie-break list?
questions.note: Shipped in Ainalrami 0.30.0: --players, --rounds, --full-bye-pct, --half-bye-pct, --zero-bye-pct, --forfeit-win-pct, --double-forfeit-pct, --odd-results-pct, --acceleration=baku, --tie-breaks (cli.ex:432-458,1510-1525; generator.ex:450-534). Percentages, not per round (optional).

questions.asks: Unset generator parameters get sensible random values?
questions.note: FAIL on a strict reading. Players, rounds and ratings are random when unset, but unset byes, forfeits, odd results, Baku and the tie-break list always fall back to none/0 (generator.ex:73,80,412,433-448,496-504,541), and the help text says unset options are random (cli.ex:1510). Fix in Ainalrami: draw them at random, keep a flag for the old corpus defaults.

questions.asks: Generator has at least one way to set ratings?
questions.note: Random ratings.

questions.asks: Generator ratings user-specified?
questions.note: --ratings=2400,2350,... per TPN (cli.ex:236-257; generator.ex:414-419). Ainalrami 0.30.0.

questions.asks: Generator ratings parametrised (min/max, gaps)?
questions.note: --rating-range=LOW-HIGH, or --rating-top/--rating-step/--rating-sigma (cli.ex:259-279; generator.ex:421-425). Ainalrami 0.30.0.

questions.asks: Generator ratings random?
questions.note: Uniform 1400..2700 from the seeded RNG when no rating option is given (generator.ex:412).

questions.asks: Same parameters always give the same TRF?
questions.note: Our answer is NO, but at risk: without --seed the seed is :erlang.unique_integer (generator.ex:66-67), a per-VM counter - eight fresh runs gave seeds 2690-2700, 2690 three times, so two -g runs can write identical files and a tester would answer YES (FAIL). Fix in Ainalrami: seed from :crypto.strong_rand_bytes.

questions.asks: Generated tournaments follow the pairing rules AND the tie-break list in the file?
questions.note: Every round is paired by the engine; with --tie-breaks the file carries 202 and final ranks by Ainalrami.Tiebreaks (generator.ex:114-129,541-558). The generator writes the engine dialect (XXR), not TRF26.

questions.asks: Generated results follow FIDE rating-table probabilities?
questions.note: --results=fide [--draw-rate] draws results from the rating table, but it is opt-in (uniform by default) and uses the uncapped table, not the 400-point rule (generator.ex:433-448,466-490), so wide rating gaps drift. Costs 5%. Fix in Ainalrami.

questions.asks: Tested against another public engine, 50,000+ tournaments each way, pairings AND tie-breaks?
questions.note: Pairings both ways against bbpPairings and tie-breaks both ways against TieBreakServer, over 50,000 tournaments each way (deps/ainalrami/docs/validation.md:17,20,24,1429-1440,1592-1606).

questions.asks: More than 10 discrepancies either way?
questions.note: YES: pairings differ twice (bbpPairings' own [C2] defect), but tie-breaks differ 147,873 times in direction 1 and 2,039 in direction 2, every one classified as a TieBreakServer finding (A-D) or a reading difference (validation.md:17,1605-1606; docs/finding-tiebreakserver-2026-09.md). Routes through Q35-Q39.

questions.asks: Discrepancies caused by our engine?
questions.note: No group of discrepancies was traced to our engines (validation.md; finding-tiebreakserver-2026-09.md).

questions.asks: Discrepancies caused by the other engine?
questions.note: Yes: bbpPairings' [C2] defect, Gacrux's 5.2.5 and TieBreakServer's findings A-D.

questions.asks: Other-engine faults reported?
questions.note: Gacrux 5.2.5 went to TEC in the 2026-09-08 letter. No record in the repository that TieBreakServer's findings A-D or bbpPairings' [C2] were sent to TEC or the authors - send them and keep the proof, or this is NO (25%).

questions.asks: Discrepancies from different readings of the rules?
questions.note: Yes: some tie-break differences are readings, not errors (e.g. STD), per finding-tiebreakserver-2026-09.md.

questions.asks: Reading differences reported to TEC?
questions.note: Only covered if the tie-break reading differences go to TEC; the 2026-09-08 letter predates them. NO costs 50%.

questions.asks: FIDE mode is the default?
questions.note: Every departing setting ships at the FIDE value (compliance.ex @departures) and a new tournament is Swiss. Caveat: an account can set Keizer as its own default (user_live/settings.ex:939); those tournaments start outside FIDE mode, stamped round 0.

questions.asks: A way to enter FIDE mode?
questions.note: Not needed: default.

questions.asks: Can the program leave FIDE mode?
questions.note: Three ways out: saving a departing setting (tournaments.ex stamp_compliance_loss), a pairing moved by soft rules, extra points or a bye exclusion (pairing.ex record_pairing_deviations), and Leave FIDE mode on Settings > FIDE (tournaments.ex:928).

questions.asks: Level-4 warning when leaving FIDE mode?
questions.note: FAIL. Only the explicit way out has TEC's Level-4 two-step confirmation (settings_fide_live.ex:85-131,179). Saving a departing setting saves at once and the notice follows; a pairing moved by soft rules, extra points or a bye exclusion leaves with an inline note only.

questions.asks: ### comment in the TRF when leaving FIDE mode?
questions.note: The TRF26 export writes '### FIDE mode exited @ Round N' (or 'before Round 1 was paired') after the header whenever fide_compliance_lost_round is set (trf_export.ex; test/pairings_engine/fide_mode_locks_test.exs) - in copies and TRF26 downloads, not in the file sent for rating, which holds only records by the arbiter's decision (SWAR parity).

questions.asks: Can FIDE mode be re-entered?
questions.note: fide_compliance_lost_round is never cleared, a restore only moves it earlier (tournament_import.ex earliest_compliance_loss), and Compliance.fide_mode?/1 needs it nil (compliance.ex:326). Caveat: a JSON backup import takes the file's value.

questions.asks: Permanent indication when not in FIDE mode?
questions.note: Every page of a tournament not in FIDE mode carries a 'Not in FIDE mode' line linking to Settings > FIDE (layouts.ex:444; fide_mode_live_test.exs).

questions.asks: Imports TRF06?
questions.note: One parser covers TRF06-era files; old-style byes are read as byes (deps/ainalrami/lib/ainalrami/trf.ex:2005-2010; trf_import.ex:1136-1147).

questions.asks: Reports every adjustment TRF06 -> TRF26?
questions.note: Costs 3%. A TRF06 file brings no 162/192/202/142, so scoring, system, tie-breaks and length take defaults silently, and old byes are converted silently; the version is not reported (trf_import.ex:539-570,587-589,1136-1147).

questions.asks: Imports TRF16?
questions.note: TrfImport.import_text/2 over Ainalrami.Trf.parse (trf_import.ex:71-76).

questions.asks: Reports every adjustment TRF16 -> TRF26?
questions.note: Costs 7%. Without 162/192/202/212/142 the import defaults silently; notes exist only for rule widening, future full-point byes, whole-field 299 and non-Baku acceleration (trf_import.ex:539-570,686-736).

questions.asks: Imports a defective TRF anyway?
questions.note: Defects are imported: dangling opponents become byes, a wrong points column is a warning, illegal rounds are imported as recorded (trf_import.ex:1136-1147,1437-1458,1498-1504).

questions.asks: Tells the user every adjustment made?
questions.note: Costs 70%. Not reported: dangling opponents turned into byes, F/U byes merged, unknown tie-breaks dropped, round-robin cycles over 2 clamped, unknown 192 codes ignored, deputies over 4 dropped, 362 P/A ignored, 299 switching on counted extra points (which leaves FIDE mode at the next pairing), a crashed verification pass swallowed (trf_import.ex:714-736,755,1136-1147,1294-1296,1534-1540).

questions.asks: Shows the issues when a TRF26 cannot be imported?
questions.note: Off our path (Q51 YES). A refused file shows why: parse error, duplicate ranks, several 012 lines, validation text (trf_import.ex:149-157,318-396).

questions.asks: Checks imported rounds against the pairing rules?
questions.note: Every imported round is replayed: explain_round, Alternatives.violations, bye_eligibility (trf_import.ex:1530-1533,1584-1653). Limits: absolute criteria only, Dutch files only.

questions.asks: Level-3 warning AND ### when imported rounds broke the rules?
questions.note: Costs 30%. The findings arrive as a flash after the tournament is committed: no confirm/cancel, no ###, nothing stored (tournaments_live.ex:1272-1279,1423-1449).

questions.asks: In FIDE mode automatically after import?
questions.note: No import sets a departing setting (trf_import.ex:539-570,686-712). Risk: positive 299 records switch on counted extra points, and the next pairing then leaves FIDE mode (pairing.ex record_pairing_deviations).

questions.asks: Round count changeable after the start?
questions.note: In FIDE mode the number of rounds (and a round robin's cycles) cannot change once round 1 is paired, and Unlock does not open it (tournaments.ex:894 @fide_locked, ensure_unlocked/3:1036; fide_mode_locks_test.exs). Leaving FIDE mode first is the way to change it.

questions.asks: Level-4 warning on that change?
questions.note: Off our path: the change cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q57), so YES by the legend.

questions.asks: ### for the change?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q57).

questions.asks: Re-checks the last round when its final/non-final status flips?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q57).

questions.asks: Level-3 + ### if that makes pairings wrong?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q57). YES itself costs 7% if reached.

questions.asks: Warns before start if the setup cannot finish within the rules?
questions.note: Costs 3%. The setup checklist checks name, rounds, dates and tie-breaks, never players against rounds (tournament.ex:1803-1812); the arbiter learns at the first round that cannot pair.

questions.asks: Manual/semi-automatic pairing to finish such a tournament?
questions.note: FAIL (was YES). When the engine finds no legal pairing nothing is paired and no round exists (pairing.ex:3052-3061); swaps and pool pairing work only inside an existing round (tournaments.ex pair_from_pool), so such a tournament cannot be finished.

questions.asks: Pairings can be created or edited by hand?
questions.note: Swap seats or colours, substitute from the pool, vacate/fill a seat, award a bye, pair two pool players, delete an empty last board - each confirmed as a board diff (tournaments.ex swap_players_in_round, pair_from_pool; pairings_live.ex:638-804).

questions.asks: Clear start and end of a manual-alteration session?
questions.note: FAIL. Each hand edit is its own staged gesture; there is no session with an end at which a check could run (pairings_live.ex:1303-1352).

questions.asks: Level-3 on rematch / prohibited / ineligible PAB / triple colour during MPA?
questions.note: Costs 25%. The confirm modals show the board diff only; no check for a rematch, a prohibited pair, PAB eligibility, three same colours or an imbalance over 2 (pairings_live.ex:1354-1546).

questions.asks: Warning when both players get the wrong colour?
questions.note: Costs 10%. No comparison with the colour each player was due (pairings_live.ex:1354-1387).

questions.asks: Check at the end of the session against the correct pairings?
questions.note: FAIL. No checker runs after hand edits; the explanation page only notes the boards diverged (round_explanation.ex:434-464).

questions.asks: Level-3 + ### when they differ?
questions.note: Costs 30%. No warning, no ###, nothing stamped (trf_export.ex).

questions.asks: Standard 1/0.5/0 scoring by default?
questions.note: 1 / 0.5 / 0, bye 1 by default (tournament.ex:106-109).

questions.asks: Other scoring systems definable?
questions.note: Free win/draw/loss values on Settings > Scoring (settings_scoring_live.ex:257-291).

questions.asks: 3-1-0 definable?
questions.note: 3-1-0 can be typed in; standings read the values live (standings.ex:1154-1156).

questions.asks: Custom scoring definable?
questions.note: Any value per result (tournament.ex:1045-1048).

questions.asks: Can two draws be worth more than a win plus a loss?
questions.note: Two draws worth more than a win plus a loss is a Compliance departure (:draws_outscore_win, compliance.ex:273): saving it takes the tournament out of FIDE mode, so in FIDE mode it cannot be set (fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Scoring changeable during the tournament?
questions.note: In FIDE mode the scoring (team match points included) cannot change once round 1 is paired; no Unlock (tournaments.ex:894, ensure_unlocked/3; settings_scoring_live.ex disabled inputs; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Re-checks already-paired rounds after a scoring change?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q75).

questions.asks: Level-3 + ### if that makes pairings wrong?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q75). YES itself costs 7% if reached.

questions.asks: Points already played follow the new scoring?
questions.note: Points are worked out from the stored results with the current values on every read (standings.ex:644-663,1154-1156; standings_cache.ex keyed by the tournament).

questions.asks: PAB can be worth a win?
questions.note: bye_value, 1.0 by default (tournament.ex:109; standings.ex:655).

questions.asks: PAB can differ from a win?
questions.note: Its own input on Settings > Scoring (settings_scoring_live.ex:284-291).

questions.asks: PAB can be worth MORE than a win?
questions.note: A bye worth more than a win is a departure (:bye_above_win, compliance.ex:276), so not in FIDE mode (fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: PAB can differ from both win and draw?
questions.note: 0 or any value below a win is allowed (settings_scoring_live.ex:285-290).

questions.asks: Standard scoring with a PAB other than 1, 0.5, 0?
questions.note: Under 1-1/2-0 a bye other than 1, 1/2 or 0 is a departure (:bye_not_a_game_score, compliance.ex:279) (fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Non-standard scoring: PAB values reachable by standard results?
questions.note: Free value: 2 under 3-1-0 stays in FIDE mode (fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: PAB value changeable during the tournament?
questions.note: In FIDE mode the bye's value (and SWAR presence points on it) cannot change once round 1 is paired; no Unlock (tournaments.ex:894; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Re-checks paired rounds after a PAB change?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q85).

questions.asks: Level-3 + ### if that makes pairings wrong?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q85). YES itself costs 7% if reached.

questions.asks: Earlier PABs re-scored to the new value?
questions.note: Every PAB is scored at the current value on every read (standings.ex:655,1055-1101).

questions.asks: Pairing systems besides the Dutch?
questions.note: Round robin (Berger), team round robin, team Swiss C.04.6; Keizer leaves FIDE mode (tournament.ex:5,14).

questions.asks: Other Swiss systems?
questions.note: Team Swiss C.04.6 through Ainalrami.TeamPairing (team_swiss.ex). The only individual Swiss is the Dutch.

questions.asks: Swiss system without a TAPC selectable?
questions.note: C.04.6 can be selected and no program is known to hold a C.04.6 TAPC; YES only routes to Q92.

questions.asks: Rules printable/obtainable for a non-Handbook Swiss system?
questions.note: Every Swiss selectable in FIDE mode is in the Handbook (Dutch, C.04.6); Keizer is not a Swiss and leaves FIDE mode.

questions.asks: Pairing system changeable once underway?
questions.note: pairing_system freezes with round 1 and in FIDE mode Unlock does not open it (tournaments.ex:894, ensure_unlocked/3; settings_options_live.ex locked_hint_message with fide_path; fide_mode_live_test.exs).

questions.asks: Round robin selectable?
questions.note: 'Round robin (Berger)' is a FIDE pairing system here (compliance.ex).

questions.asks: Round-robin TPNs assignable by hand?
questions.note: FAIL (was YES). Round-robin numbers are frozen at the first pairing by rating then name (round_robin.ex:389-393; pairing.ex:633-660); no page sets them and there is no draw-of-lots entry. Only a TRF or SWAR import can set them.

questions.asks: Berger tables?
questions.note: Circle-method Berger tables, single and double, checked against C.05 Annex 1 and SWAR's generator (round_robin.ex:8-45,256-270).

questions.asks: Manual round-robin pairing (no Berger)?
questions.note: Not reached: Q96 YES.

questions.asks: Double RR: choose whether to reverse the last two rounds of cycle 1?
questions.note: Cycle 2 is cycle 1 with colours reversed, same order; no option for the last-two-rounds swap (round_robin.ex:256-270). Routes to Q99.

questions.asks: Always reverses those two rounds?
questions.note: Costs 10%. The last two rounds of cycle 1 are never reversed for an even field (round_robin.ex:264-269), so three same colours in a row can happen across the cycle boundary.

questions.asks: Manual round-robin pairing possible?
questions.note: Costs 7%. A round-robin round cannot be generated by hand; Pair always builds the Berger schedule (pairings_live.ex:1897-1900).

questions.asks: Checks each pair meets once/twice?
questions.note: Off our path while Q100 is NO; hand edits are not checked for meeting everyone once/twice (costs 15% if reached).

questions.asks: Non-Berger double RR: no three same colours?
questions.note: Round robins are always generated from Berger tables, so the non-Berger case cannot arise (round_robin.ex:256-270).

questions.asks: RR standings exclude results of players under 50% of games?
questions.note: FAIL. Nothing removes the results of a round-robin player who completed under 50% of games; their games count for everyone's score and tie-breaks (standings.ex:141-161; round_robin.ex:459-463).

questions.asks: RR tie-breaks (DE, BPG, BWG, REP, STD, SB, SB/C1-2, RTNG, WIN, TPN, KS variants) correct?
questions.note: Present: DE, BPG, SB, WIN, KS. Missing from the catalogue and the bridge: BWG, REP, STD, SB/C1, SB/C2, RTNG, RTNG/R, TPN, TPN/R, KS/L1, KS/L2, KS/L-1, KS/L-2 (tiebreaks.ex:31-150; standings/ainalrami_bridge.ex:44-58). Ainalrami computes them all. The draft gives NO no outcome, only that all must be implemented: treat as a failure.

questions.asks: Buchholz-type tie-breaks usable in RR?
questions.note: Buchholz-type codes can be picked but standings drop them for a round robin and say why (standings.ex:153-160; tiebreaks.ex:174-185); FB/AOB do not exist. They still appear in the TRF's 202 list.

questions.asks: Baku acceleration correct?
questions.note: FAIL (was YES). In the accelerated rounds the app orders each bracket by game points, then rating, then TPN, without the virtual points (pairing.ex order_for_pairing:4444), so a group-A player who lost sits below a group-B player who won in the same pairing-score bracket - C.04.7 ranks by pairing score, then TPN. Measured 2026-10-02: in 7 of 7 random Baku tournaments rounds 2-3 differ from `ainalrami -c`'s replay of our own TRF; adding round R's virtual points to that order made 10 of 10 match. Group A itself is right (2*ceil(n/4) by TPN, pairing.ex:4106-4136); see Q111 for late entrants.

questions.asks: Other acceleration methods?
questions.note: Only none/Baku in FIDE mode; extra points as acceleration is a departure (pairing.ex pairing_deviations).

questions.asks: Rules for other methods printable?
questions.note: Off our path (Q107 NO): no other method in FIDE mode.

questions.asks: Acceleration removable after round 1?
questions.note: In FIDE mode acceleration freezes with round 1, no Unlock (tournaments.ex:894; settings_options_live.ex disabled select; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Acceleration changeable after round 1?
questions.note: Same lock as Q109.

questions.asks: Percentage groups respect round-1 byes having no TPN?
questions.note: Costs 35%. Every active player gets a TPN at round 1, round-1 byes and late entrants included, and all count towards the Baku group size (pairing.ex:235-237,4115-4124,4479-4485), against the SPP's 2026-08-27 reading of C.04.2:2.4.

questions.asks: All pairing-integrity events logged?
questions.note: Costs 15% (was YES). The audit trail records the raw acts (result changes with their round, confirmed postponed non-draws, every hand edit, settings diffs) but nothing is identified as a PIBE, import findings are not stored, and no checker runs on hand edits (pairings_live.ex:953-972; tournaments_live.ex:1272-1277).

questions.asks: PIBEs written to the TRF as ###?
questions.note: Off our path while Q112 is NO; no PIBE is written as ###.

questions.asks: A PIBE can be undone automatically?
questions.note: Costs 3%. Restore points are taken before pairing, unpairing, a match forfeit, a CSV import and a hand-off, not before a correction, a postponed result, a hand edit or a settings change (pairings_live.ex:525,1209-1214,1906-1911).

questions.asks: Level-3 before finalising a PIBE?
questions.note: Costs 10%. Hand edits and postponed non-draws are confirmed first; a previous-round correction and an import are not (pairings_live.ex:953-972; tournaments_live.ex:1272-1277).

questions.asks: Separate official vs tournament rating?
questions.note: fide_rating is the official rating (TRF 001); the pairing rating is fide_rating, or national_rating when there is none (player.ex:12-16,728-736). Weak YES: a FIDE-rated player cannot get a separate tournament rating.

questions.asks: Custom rating lists?
questions.note: Costs 18%. Only the FIDE list and the KBSB list, each from a fixed source; no custom list (fide/sync.ex:35,51-53).

questions.asks: Effective Rapid/Blitz lists?
questions.note: rating_for_tempo falls back to the standard rating when rapid or blitz is missing - the Effective Rapid/Blitz lists (fide.ex:133-141; rating_refresh.ex:83).

questions.asks: Type-A lists (known source)?
questions.note: FIDE list from ratings.fide.com, KBSB list from the federation's public file (fide/sync.ex:1-5,35; federations/bel/sync.ex:77).

questions.asks: Type-B lists (unknown source)?
questions.note: Off our path. No list of unknown origin can be imported.

questions.asks: All official FIDE lists as Type-A?
questions.note: The combined players_list.zip brings standard, rapid and blitz in one sync (fide/sync.ex:103-135; fide/fide_player.ex:9-11).

questions.asks: All official FIDE lists importable as Type-B?
questions.note: Off our path (only from Q120 YES).

questions.asks: Default rating-list sequence per tournament type?
questions.note: Costs 7%. One list per rate of play, no sequence (std has no rapid/blitz fallback) (fide.ex:135-141).

questions.asks: User can define/modify the sequence?
questions.note: No sequence to define; routes to Q125 (fide.ex:133-141).

questions.asks: Only one list at a time?
questions.note: One FIDE list per tournament, picked by its rate of play, plus the national fallback (fide.ex:135-141; player.ex:728-736).

questions.asks: Sequence editable (exclude, add, reorder)?
questions.note: Off our path (only from Q123 YES).

questions.asks: Rating auto-assigned from the main list?
questions.note: Picking a FIDE search result fills the rating for the tournament's rate of play (players_live.ex:645-670; fide.ex:135).

questions.asks: Shows ratings in other lists when not in the main one?
questions.note: Costs 7%. The add-player results show only the standard rating, and nothing flags a missing main-list rating (players_live.ex:2412-2423).

questions.asks: User can pick one of those?
questions.note: Off our path while Q128 is NO; other-list ratings are display-only in the edit dialog.

questions.asks: Minimum rating entered automatically when none found?
questions.note: No automatic minimum rating (player.ex:13,728-736); routes to Q131.

questions.asks: Rating enterable by hand?
questions.note: Free FIDE and national rating inputs on the add form (players_live.ex:2460,2484).

questions.asks: Assigned rating editable?
questions.note: Editable in the edit dialog at any time (players_live.ex:3194,3199).

questions.asks: Consistency checks (are ratings still current)?
questions.note: Refresh ratings re-looks-up every player by FIDE ID and proposes each difference (rating_refresh.ex:60-88).

questions.asks: Source list kept per rating, and manual entry marked?
questions.note: Costs 18%. No source list, list date or manual marker is stored per rating (player.ex:12-16).

questions.asks: Local FIDE lists never more than a day old while running?
questions.note: Costs 18%. The FIDE sync runs only from the admin's button; no scheduler (fide_live.ex:327-333).

questions.asks: One-click update of all local lists?
questions.note: One sync replaces standard, rapid and blitz together (fide_live.ex:327-333).

questions.asks: Consistency check uses the list valid at start (or check date if >30 days)?
questions.note: Costs 7%. The check uses the latest synced list, whatever the start date; the list period is not recorded (rating_refresh.ex:60-91).

questions.asks: Consistency checks can be switched on/off?
questions.note: Off our path (Q137 NO skips it). No switch for consistency checks.

questions.asks: Automatic consistency check after a list update?
questions.note: Nothing runs a check after a sync (fide/sync.ex:209-224); routes to Q140.

questions.asks: Consistency check only on request?
questions.note: Costs 25%. The check runs only when the arbiter presses Refresh ratings (players_live.ex:983-986).

questions.asks: Checks the lists are current before a requested check?
questions.note: Costs 18%. The check never compares the local list's date with FIDE's before running (players_live.ex:983-986).

questions.asks: Affected players reported?
questions.note: Each affected player with old and new values (players_live.ex:2829-2858).

questions.asks: Ratings updated automatically?
questions.note: Nothing is written until Apply (players_live.ex:992-1004).

questions.asks: User can update a chosen subset?
questions.note: Costs 12%. Apply takes every proposal; no subset (players_live.ex:992-995).

questions.asks: Tournament-rating methods FIDE/NRO/FIDON/NIDOF/HBFN/OTHER?
questions.note: Costs 117% - the draft prices each missing method: FIDE 70, NRO 30, NIDOF 7, HBFN 7, OTHER 3. Only FIDON exists, hard-coded: FIDE rating if any, else national (player.ex:727-736; pairing.ex:670).

questions.asks: Tie order beyond alphabetical for equal rating/title?
questions.note: Costs 15%. Equal ratings are ordered by name only; the FIDE title is not used (pairing.ex:670).

questions.asks: TPNs changeable without editing ratings?
questions.note: Costs 7%. No page sets a TPN; numbers are issued at round 1 and frozen (player.ex:166; pairing.ex:633-658). Routes to Q155.

questions.asks: TPN exchange only among equal tournament ratings?
questions.note: Off our path (Q147 NO); there is no TPN exchange.

questions.asks: Level-3 when an exchange breaks the seeding rules?
questions.note: Off our path; vacuous - no exchange exists.

questions.asks: Level-3 on any TPN exchange?
questions.note: Off our path; vacuous - no exchange exists.

questions.asks: TPN exchange/regeneration after round 4 paired?
questions.note: Off our path. Changing a number after round 4 is paired is refused (tournaments.ex guard_pairing_number_freeze).

questions.asks: Level-4 if so?
questions.note: Off our path (Q151 NO).

questions.asks: TPN regeneration before round 4?
questions.note: Off our path today (Q147 NO); no regeneration exists, and NO costs 60% if reached.

questions.asks: Level-3 when regeneration moves two or more TPNs?
questions.note: Off our path; vacuous.

questions.asks: Regeneration keeps the tie-order chosen at first?
questions.note: Vacuous: no regeneration and no arbiter-set tie order to keep (pairing.ex:670).

questions.asks: Late entry after round 4 gets a correct TPN?
questions.note: Costs 18%. A late entrant always gets the next free number, never the TPN their rating gives (pairing.ex:647-658,687-693).

questions.asks: A game can be recorded as adjourned?
questions.note: With postponed games on (Settings > Scoring), *W/*B on the Pairings page, the phone and CSV (results.ex:105-113,152; tournaments.ex update_pairing_result).

questions.asks: Can it pair with results missing?
questions.note: An open * never blocks pairing; blank boards block the normal button and a second one records them as * and pairs (pairing.ex:154-183,422-430).

questions.asks: Missing results auto-recorded as adjourned?
questions.note: Confirmed blank two-player boards of the last round are written as * before pairing, and put back if the pairing fails (postponed_games.ex:244-258,349-377).

questions.asks: Level-2 warning for that?
questions.note: A confirmation before, enforced on the server, then a notice and an audit row (pairings_live.ex:3480-3510; postponed_games.ex:56). Stronger than Level 2.

questions.asks: Final standings with results missing?
questions.note: Standings shown or printed while a game has no result, or a * is open, say they are not final (Tournaments.count_missing_results/2 tournaments.ex:5185; components/postponed.ex:399; print_controller.ex postponed_banner; fide_mode_live_test.exs). Was split: blanks used to print with no warning.

questions.asks: Results for adjourned games enterable any time?
questions.note: A postponed game's result can be entered and corrected in any round; it is exempt from FIDE mode's round window (tournaments.ex:4778 ensure_result_round_open; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Level-3 when an adjourned result is not a draw?
questions.note: Replacing * with a non-draw is refused until confirmed, for every writer (postponed_games.ex:302-320; pairings_live.ex:921-929).

questions.asks: Adjourned game marked in the ITDX file?
questions.note: Open * is written as ? on both players' 001 lines in the TRF26 export (trf_export.ex).

questions.asks: Marked with ??
questions.note: ? in 001, and 162's X at the draw value so the points column adds up (trf_export.ex).

questions.asks: Unknown result symbols imported as unknown?
questions.note: Costs 10%. Only ? becomes *; any other unknown code is refused by Ainalrami's parser (trf_import.ex:1074-1075; deps/ainalrami/lib/ainalrami/trf.ex:83-88,1958-1961).

questions.asks: Provisional score other than a draw allowed?
questions.note: Draw by default; win or loss only as a departure (compliance.ex :postponed_*_not_draw).

questions.asks: Level-2 when pairing with an older adjourned game open?
questions.note: A confirmation naming the open games before pairing, enforced on the server (postponed_games.ex:261-273; pairing.ex:154-166).

questions.asks: Final standings/TRF with an adjourned game open?
questions.note: FAIL on the draft's reading. With a * open the TRF26 can be downloaded and finalised for sending (the game goes out as ?) and standings are produced, marked not final (postponed_games.ex:726-774; trf_export.ex). This is the project's design for games played after the event (reported as their own FIDE tournament); see the open questions.

questions.asks: Withdrawal shown in the standings?
questions.note: Costs 7%. No withdrawn marker on the standings page or print (standings_live.ex:916-924; print_controller.ex:1027-1066).

questions.asks: Non-zero score for an unpaired player?
questions.note: Absences score abs_value, the PAB bye_value (standings.ex:644-680).

questions.asks: Half-point bye?
questions.note: A half-point bye is an absence with absence points at 1/2 (standings.ex:662,674-680); written as H, the half-point bye, by Pairing.unplayed_code/2 (it was Z with 162 Z=0.5 until 2026-10-02).

questions.asks: Two or more half-point byes?
questions.note: Unlimited unless abs_nbfois caps it (standings.ex:674-691).

questions.asks: Level-3 on the second and later half-point bye?
questions.note: Costs 15%. A second paid absence raises no warning (tournaments.ex update_player; players_live.ex:3353).

questions.asks: Players can be marked ineligible for half-point byes?
questions.note: Costs 7%. No half-point-bye-ineligible flag (player.ex:53-61). Routes to Q177.

questions.asks: HPB assignable to an ineligible player?
questions.note: Off our path (Q175 NO).

questions.asks: Full-point bye assignable?
questions.note: Costs 7%. No full-point bye: a vacancy bye is stored and exported as a PAB (tournaments.ex award_bye_for_vacancy; pairing.ex:4960-4964). Routes to Q180.

questions.asks: Level-2 saying full-point byes are deprecated?
questions.note: Off our path (Q177 NO).

questions.asks: ### for a full-point bye?
questions.note: Off our path (Q177 NO); costs 3% once a full-point bye exists without a ### line.

questions.asks: Odd over-the-board results (1/2-0, 0-1/2, 0-0)?
questions.note: 1/2-0, 0-1/2 and 0-0 can be entered (results.ex:94-99,152).

questions.asks: Inconsistent results (1-1/2, 1-1)?
questions.note: Only codes in the Results table are accepted; 1-1 and 1-1/2 do not exist (results.ex:89-114).

questions.asks: Invalid forfeits (1/2F-0F ...)?
questions.note: No drawn forfeit code (results.ex:96-98).

questions.asks: Only 1F-0F, 0F-1F, 0F-0F as forfeits?
questions.note: Only 1-0FF, 0-1FF and 0-0FF (results.ex:96-98,152).

questions.asks: Mixed standard/forfeit results?
questions.note: No code mixes a played result with a forfeit (results.ex:89-114).

questions.asks: Unrated results (game under one move)?
All enterable results handled correctly?
questions.note: One classification table drives standings, tie-breaks, engine input, export and import (results.ex:89-114).

questions.asks: Boards ordered by the published rules?
questions.note: Costs 7%. Individual Swiss boards come in the engine's output order, not sorted by C.04.2:3.6 (pairing.ex:826-832); only team Swiss sorts (team_swiss.ex:213-235).

questions.asks: With acceleration, ordered by real + fictitious points?
questions.note: Off our path (Q187 NO). Include Baku's virtual points when Q187 is built, or this costs 3%.

questions.asks: Can results/pairings/colours of ANY earlier round be changed?
questions.note: In FIDE mode only the round before the last played, and later ones, can be changed: results, hand edits, team forfeit decisions, and deleting a player who played a closed round are refused (Tournaments.ensure_round_editable/2 tournaments.ex:5168, sent_round_gate/2:5116, ensure_result_round_open/2:4778; team_matches.ex:153; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Of the round before the last one played?
questions.note: The round before the last played stays open (tournaments.ex:5168; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Of rounds before the second-to-last?
questions.note: Rounds before the second-to-last played are closed in FIDE mode (tournaments.ex:5168; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Corrections recorded for the rating report only (C.04.2:4.3)?
questions.note: Costs 15%. No rating-only correction: a board has one result for standings, pairing and TRF (tournaments/pairing.ex).

questions.asks: ### noting results used differ from 001 records?
questions.note: Off our path while Q192 is NO.

questions.asks: Prohibited pairings supported?
questions.note: Prohibited pairs and club/federation exclusions for the whole tournament, written as 260 (tournaments.ex add_forbidden_pairing; trf_export.ex). No per-round prohibition.

questions.asks: Only before round 1 is paired?
questions.note: FAIL. Prohibitions can be added at any time (tournaments.ex add_forbidden_pairing). Disputed: our 2026-09-08 letter (docs/tec-feedback-2026-09.md:179-193, B.6) argues C.05:5.2 binds the organiser, not the software. See the open questions.

questions.asks: Addable after a round has been played?
questions.note: FAIL. Same: added after a round with no warning; the club/federation exclusion settings are not frozen either.

questions.asks: Expelled player can be flagged?
questions.note: Costs 3%. Player status is active or withdrawn; no expelled flag (player.ex:19,189).

questions.asks: Expelled player excluded from standings?
questions.note: Costs 2%. Every player is ranked; no exclusion from the standings (standings.ex:248,289-298).

questions.asks: All Swiss tie-breaks in C.07 usable (AOB, APPO, APRO, ARO cuts/medians, BH/FB cuts/medians, BPG, BWG, DE, DE/P, PS cuts, PTP, REP, RTNG, SB cuts, STD, TPN, TPR, WIN, WON)?
questions.note: 12 of the 39 can be selected: ARO, ARO/C1, BH, BH/C1, BH/C2, BH/M1, BPG, DE, PS, SB, WIN, WON. Missing: AOB, AOB/F, APPO, APRO, ARO/C2, ARO/M1, ARO/M2, BH/M2, BWG, DE/P, FB, FB/C1, FB/C2, FB/M1, FB/M2, PS/C1, PS/C2, PTP, REP, RTNG, RTNG/R, SB/C1, SB/C2, STD, TPN, TPN/R, TPR (tiebreaks.ex:32-155; ainalrami_bridge.ex:44-57). Ainalrami computes all of them. The draft gives NO no outcome, only that all must be implemented: treat as a failure.

questions.asks: Tie-break list changeable during the tournament?
questions.note: In FIDE mode the tie-break list freezes with round 1, no Unlock (tournaments.ex:894; settings_tournament_live.ex disabled editor; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Level-4 on that change?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q200).

questions.asks: ### with round and previous list?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q200).

questions.asks: Ties allowed at the end?
questions.note: Costs 15% (was YES). Players still level after C.07 are ordered by rating, name and id and numbered 1..N, so no shared place is ever shown (standings.ex:289-298,463-473).

questions.asks: Simulated drawing of lots for ties?
questions.note: Off our path (Q203 NO). No drawing of lots for tied places.

questions.asks: Tied players rankable by hand?
questions.note: Manual ranking: reseed from the computed order and move players (tournaments.ex:2812-2930).

questions.asks: Repeated drawing of lots gives different results?
questions.note: No drawing of lots exists to repeat.

questions.asks: Externally calculated tie-break values enterable?
questions.note: Costs 10%. No externally calculated tie-break values (tiebreaks.ex:32-155).

questions.asks: At least one method for unrated players in rating tie-breaks?
questions.note: Costs 32%. With any unrated player, ARO and ARO/C1 are dropped for the whole event; no handling method (standings.ex:61-63,141-161). Ainalrami's /U<rating> is not wired in.

questions.asks: More than one such method?
questions.note: Off our path while Q208 is NO.

questions.asks: Flag for tournaments over 30 days?
questions.note: Costs 40%. No flag for a tournament over 30 days, one rating per player (player.ex:13-15). Routes to Q217.

questions.asks: Advises against rating tie-breaks for those (C.07:10)?
questions.note: Off our path (Q210 NO).

questions.asks: Several ratings per player for long events?
questions.note: Off our path (Q210 NO).

questions.asks: Ratings linked to rounds?
questions.note: Off our path (Q210 NO).

questions.asks: Rating tie-breaks per round's rating?
questions.note: Off our path (Q210 NO).

questions.asks: Default first rating (C.07:10)?
questions.note: Off our path (Q210 NO).

questions.asks: User chooses which rating?
questions.note: Off our path (Q210 NO).

questions.asks: Final TRF reflects everything that happened, no TRF-defined event left out?
questions.note: Costs 30%. Since 2026-10-02 the rank column (86-89) is the place, not the starting rank, and 202 uses C.07's spelling (BH/C1, BH/M1, ARO/C1) - before, `ainalrami -c` called nearly every place wrong or could not check the standings at all (trf_export.ex with_final_ranks, tie_break_codes; trf_checker_round_trip_test.exs). Still not written: 152 (the initial colour drawn by lot), 212, 172, 330, scoped 299, 222 for DELAY or free text; no ### for corrections or late prohibitions (trf_export.ex). The FIDE-mode exit line is written (Q44).

questions.asks: Level-2 warnings can be switched off?
questions.note: No setting turns warnings off (postponed_games.ex:54-79; features.ex:108-180).

questions.asks: Level-2 and 3 warnings can be switched off?
questions.note: Confirmations are enforced in the write path; no switch skips them (postponed_games.ex:328-337).

questions.asks: Level-4 warnings can be switched off?
questions.note: No setting disables a confirmation (postponed_games.ex:328-337).

questions.asks: Level-4 can be relaxed to Level-3?
questions.note: The warnings are fixed in code (postponed_games.ex:54-79).

questions.asks: Chess960 supported?
questions.note: Costs 15%. No Chess960: no variant setting and no draw of the start position.

questions.asks: Usable without an internet connection?
questions.note: Desktop releases run locally. Verification ends here.

questions.asks: Controlled offline test environment offered?
questions.note: Not reached.

questions.asks: All checks possible in that environment?
questions.note: Not reached.
